Only after the deterministic timing calculation confirms the failure may the letter state that the NTK was not given within the statutory period for the postal route, so keeper liability is not established under Schedule 4.
Multiple visits / double visit. Require review of the complete ANPR sequence rather than two selected images. Keeper-safe - 'the vehicle attended on more than one occasion'.

The operator has not established the identity of the driver. As the applicable Schedule 4 requirements have also not been satisfied, liability cannot be transferred to the registered keeper under Schedule 4.

For the verified reasons set out above, the operator has not established keeper liability under Schedule 4 of the Protection of Freedoms Act 2012. The charge should therefore be cancelled as against the registered keeper.

actual.letter:
I write as the registered keeper of vehicle AB12CDE in respect of Parking Charge Notice PCN123456. I dispute liability for this parking charge and require the operator to consider this appeal.

The Parking Charge Notice alleges: Overstayed paid time at Retail Park.

On the operator's own documents the parking event took place on 1 June 2026, the Notice to Keeper was issued on 20 June 2026; the statutory period for delivery of the notice ended on 15 June 2026 and it is deemed delivered on 23 June 2026, 8 days outside that period, so the notice was not delivered within the statutory period and keeper liability does not transfer.

The Notice to Keeper was not delivered within the applicable statutory period for the relevant postal-notice route. The operator has therefore failed to satisfy a condition required to transfer liability to the registered keeper under Schedule 4.

The operator has not established the identity of the driver. As the applicable Schedule 4 requirements have also not been satisfied, liability cannot be transferred to the registered keeper under Schedule 4.

The vehicle attended the location on more than one separate occasion. The first recorded entry and final recorded exit must not be treated as one continuous parking event without review of the complete sequence.

The operator should review the complete sequence of captures for the vehicle and date, including intermediate entry/exit records, rather than relying only on the two images reproduced on the PCN.

For the reasons set out above, the parking charge is disputed and the operator is requested to cancel the Parking Charge Notice.

The operator has not established the identity of the driver. As the applicable Schedule 4 requirements have also not been satisfied, liability cannot be transferred to the registered keeper under Schedule 4. For the verified reasons set out above, the operator has not established keeper liability under Schedule 4 of the Protection of Freedoms Act 2012. The charge should therefore be cancelled as against the registered keeper. If the operator is not prepared to cancel the charge, it is requested to provide a clear response addressing the specific grounds and evidence raised.
